paragraphs: These terms and conditions govern the use of the CommonLink service by organisations that present donation fundraising campaigns on it.
They include the service's financial terms. The relationship between CommonLink and donors is governed by separate terms.
articles.title: Article 1. Purpose

paragraphs: CommonLink: the company identified at the head of these terms. Platform: the digital environment enabling campaigns to be presented, donations to be received and payments to be traced. Organisation: the association or endowment fund using the service. Campaign: the fundraising operation presented by the organisation. Donation: the payment made without consideration by a donor for the benefit of the organisation. Beneficiary: the person or entity to which the organisation pays funds as part of a campaign. Traced payment: a payment made by the organisation from the platform, recorded and published.
articles.title: Article 2. Definitions

paragraphs: Acceptance of these terms is required to use the service. It is obtained expressly upon registration, before any fundraising.
The accepted version, its date and time are retained.
articles.title: Article 3. Acceptance

paragraphs: CommonLink is a crowdfunding intermediary. Its role is to connect donors with organisations carrying projects of general interest, to enable payments to be traced, and to publish the corresponding information.
CommonLink is not a payment institution. Payment services are provided by authorised providers.
CommonLink does not direct the organisation's activity and does not act in its place in the conduct of its projects.
articles.title: Article 4. Status and role of CommonLink

paragraphs: The service is open to declared associations holding a registration number in the national register of associations, and to endowment funds, established in France.

The organisation must have a legal existence that can be verified in public registers, have its registered office in France, designate an identified legal representative, and hold a bank account opened in its name.
The organisation informs CommonLink of any change affecting these conditions.
articles.title: Article 5. Eligibility conditions

paragraphs: CommonLink verifies the existence and identity of the organisation with public registers, and carries out the checks required by its anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations.
The organisation provides the information requested and undertakes that it is accurate. No accounting document, expense receipt or activity report is requested from it.
As long as these checks are not complete, the organisation cannot collect donations.
articles.title: Article 6. Registration and checks

paragraphs: Donations are collected into a payment account opened in the organisation's name with the collection provider, whose terms are accepted by the organisation upon registration.
The organisation is the holder of this account. It retains ownership and use of it, including after these terms end.
articles.title: Article 7. Payment account

paragraphs: Payments made by the organisation from the platform are executed from its own bank account, using the payment initiation service provided by Perspecteev, trading as Bridge, a payment institution authorised by the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority under number 16918.

Each payment is authorised by the organisation's legal representative, who authenticates with their bank within Bridge's technical environment. CommonLink can neither trigger a payment in its place, nor cancel it once authorised. Bridge does not hold the funds at any point.

The data necessary for the execution of these payments is processed by Bridge as data controller, under the terms provided for in its documentation. The data processed by CommonLink is processed under the conditions set out in Article 22.
articles.title: Article 8. Outgoing payments

paragraphs: Donations never pass through CommonLink. It never receives, holds or forwards any donation, and the amounts collected never appear in its accounts at any point.
Neither CommonLink nor the payment initiation provider holds the funds at any point.
Donations vest in the organisation as soon as they are received.
articles.title: Article 9. The funds

paragraphs: The organisation creates its campaigns under its own responsibility. It is solely the author of the information it publishes there and guarantees its accuracy.
A campaign may only be published once its purpose, target amount, timetable, projected budget for the use of funds, and expected outcome have been provided. This check is automatic.
The organisation undertakes that the purpose of each campaign falls within its statutory purpose and corresponds to a need of general interest.
articles.title: Article 10. Creating a campaign

paragraphs: Campaigns may not be presented on the platform if their purpose is unlawful, if they benefit a political party, a candidate or an election campaign, if they benefit an identified person or family, if they offer consideration to the donor, if they fund the practice of a religion, if they fund the legal costs of an identified person, or if they in reality fund a commercial activity.
The full list and its detail appear on the public page devoted to transparency.
articles.title: Article 11. Excluded campaigns

paragraphs: CommonLink does not exercise any prior editorial control over campaigns and does not assess the merits of the projects presented.

A published campaign may be removed if it falls within an excluded case. The organisation is informed of the decision, may submit its observations and contest it. Each removal is recorded with its reason and date.
articles.title: Article 12. Publication and removal

paragraphs: The goal announced by a campaign constitutes a cap. When it is reached, the campaign stops accepting donations.
The goal is not a threshold for release of funds: the organisation has access to the donations received even if it is not reached.
articles.title: Article 13. Fundraising goal

paragraphs: The organisation undertakes to make, from the platform, the payments funded by the donations collected for a campaign.
This undertaking is at the heart of the service: it is what lets donors see how the amounts they paid were used.
articles.title: Article 14. Tracing of payments

paragraphs: CommonLink publishes, on the page of each campaign, the payments made by the organisation from the platform, with their recipient and amount, as well as the share of collected funds they represent.
This publication is a feature of the service, accepted by the organisation. It is factual and involves no assessment of its conduct.
The organisation may at any time add a comment explaining all or part of the untraced amount. This comment is published together with the information.
articles.title: Article 15. Publication of the use of funds

paragraphs: At the closing of a campaign, the organisation publishes a report accounting for the use of the funds collected.
If part of the funds has not been spent, the organisation states in this report what it does with them. These funds remain vested in it and are not returned to donors.
articles.title: Article 16. Closing a campaign and report

paragraphs: The organisation declares that it falls within the categories referred to in Articles 200 and 238 bis of the French General Tax Code, and that it is able to issue tax receipts. CommonLink does not verify this eligibility.

The organisation mandates CommonLink to issue and forward tax receipts in its name and on its behalf, based on the information it provides. Receipts are issued under the sole responsibility of the organisation, which is the declarant.
The organisation remains solely liable for the reporting obligations incumbent on it, in particular the annual declaration of the total amount of donations and the number of receipts issued.
articles.title: Article 17. Tax receipts

paragraphs: The organisation guarantees CommonLink against the consequences of an inaccurate declaration on its part relating to its eligibility or to the information shown on the receipts.
This guarantee is limited to those consequences. It does not cover failures attributable to CommonLink.
articles.title: Article 18. Guarantee on tax receipts

paragraphs: Donors' data is processed by CommonLink to enable donations to be made and tax receipts to be issued. The organisation accesses it for purposes related to its obligations as declarant and to its relationship with its donors.
The organisation is prohibited from any other use of this data, in particular its transfer or use for purposes unrelated to its purpose.
articles.title: Article 19. Donors' personal data

paragraphs: When the organisation puts online, on its own domain name, a collection page powered by CommonLink, it is the publisher of that page.
It includes its own legal notice there and states that the collection service is provided by CommonLink.
The data entered by donors on this page is processed under the terms agreed between the parties, set out in the appendix.
articles.title: Article 20. Collection pages hosted by the organisation

paragraphs: CommonLink receives a commission of 10% excluding tax on the amount of donations collected during the month, i.e. 12% including tax at the applicable value added tax rate.
This commission covers the whole of the service, including the fees of the collection provider, which are never re-billed to the organisation.
There is no other charge: no subscription, no set-up fee, no per-transaction fee, no transfer fee, no exit fee. There is no minimum billing amount.
articles.title: Article 21. Price

paragraphs: The commission is billed at the end of the month based on donations collected during the month. No invoice is issued for a month with no fundraising.
The invoice is paid by transfer, no later than the end of the month following that of its issue.
The commission is never deducted from donations.
A donation cancelled after billing gives rise to a correction on the following invoice.
articles.title: Article 22. Billing and payment

paragraphs: In the event of late payment, penalties are due as of right, without prior formal notice, at the interest rate applied by the European Central Bank to its most recent refinancing operation, increased by ten percentage points.

A flat-rate recovery cost indemnity of forty euros is also due for each overdue invoice. Where the recovery costs incurred exceed this amount, additional compensation may be claimed on production of supporting documents.
articles.title: Article 23. Late payment

paragraphs: CommonLink may amend its financial terms. Any amendment is notified to the organisation at least three months before it takes effect.
An organisation that does not accept the new terms may end these terms before they take effect, without charge or penalty.
articles.title: Article 24. Change in price

paragraphs: The organisation undertakes to use the service in accordance with the law and these terms, to provide accurate and up-to-date information, not to use the service for fraudulent or unlawful purposes, not to disrupt its operation, and not to circumvent its security measures.
It is responsible for the confidentiality of its users' access credentials.
articles.title: Article 25. Organisation's obligations

paragraphs: The organisation retains its rights over the content it publishes. It grants CommonLink, for the duration of these terms and for the needs of the service, the right to reproduce and display it on the platform and on campaign promotion materials.
It guarantees that it holds the rights necessary over this content, in particular over images depicting individuals.
articles.title: Article 26. Content published by the organisation

paragraphs: The platform, its names, distinctive signs, logos, editorial content and developments are protected under intellectual property law. Any unauthorised reproduction or use is prohibited.
articles.title: Article 27. CommonLink's intellectual property

paragraphs: CommonLink implements reasonable means to ensure the proper functioning of the service. It may interrupt it for maintenance, security or updates, endeavouring to inform organisations and to limit the duration.
articles.title: Article 28. Availability of the service

paragraphs: CommonLink undertakes to provide the service diligently and in a professional manner. It is subject to a best-efforts obligation, to the exclusion of any obligation of result.

The service consists of enabling the presentation of campaigns, the receipt of donations and the tracing of payments. CommonLink does not guarantee any volume of donations, the achievement of a fundraising goal, any visibility outcome, or uninterrupted availability.
CommonLink is liable for breaches of its own obligations under ordinary law. These terms neither limit nor remove the organisation's right to compensation.
articles.title: Article 29. CommonLink's undertakings and scope of the service

paragraphs: Neither party may be held liable for failure to perform its obligations resulting from a case of force majeure within the meaning of Article 1218 of the French Civil Code.
articles.title: Article 30. Force majeure

paragraphs: CommonLink may suspend all or part of access to the service in the following cases: suspected fraud or unlawful use, repeated failure to comply with the payment-tracing obligation provided for in Article 14, inaccurate or outdated registration information, loss of eligibility conditions, persistent non-payment, or where a legal obligation requires it.

The suspension is notified and reasoned. Except in the event of fraud, unlawful use or a legal obligation, it only takes effect after a period of fifteen days allowing the organisation to remedy the situation.
The organisation is informed of the measures taken, except where the law prohibits it.
articles.title: Article 31. Suspension

paragraphs: CommonLink may refuse to execute a transaction or to act on a payment request, in particular under its anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations.
articles.title: Article 32. Refusal of a transaction

paragraphs: These terms are entered into for an indefinite term, with no minimum commitment period.
The organisation may end them at any time, without reason, subject to one month's notice.
CommonLink may end them subject to one month's notice. In the event of a breach by the organisation, termination is preceded by formal notice and a period of fifteen days to remedy the situation.
CommonLink may terminate without notice in the event of fraud, unlawful use of the service, loss of eligibility conditions, or where a legal obligation requires it.
articles.title: Article 33. Term and termination

paragraphs: Ongoing campaigns are closed. The organisation publishes the report provided for in Article 16.
Donations already received remain vested in it. Ongoing recurring donations end, and the donors concerned are informed.
Campaign pages remain accessible.
The payment account opened in the organisation's name remains vested in it.
Commissions owed on donations collected before the end of the contract remain payable.

In the event of CommonLink ceasing its activity, the organisation retains its payment account, its bank account and the funds it has collected. Organisations and donors are informed in advance, and campaign pages remain accessible.

The end of the contract does not result in the immediate deletion of the organisation's data. CommonLink retains what the law requires it to keep, in particular for five years under its anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations. Once these periods expire, the data is deleted.
articles.title: Article 34. Effects of the end of the contract

paragraphs: An organisation that has not begun any fundraising may terminate its registration at any time, without reason and free of charge, by writing to contact@common-link.org. Termination is carried out within thirty days of the request and confirmed by email.
The effects provided for in Article 34 regarding data retention apply.
articles.title: Article 35. Termination of registration

paragraphs: CommonLink, 1047 Chemin des Impiniers, 06220 Vallauris, France. Phone: +33 4 23 40 02 06, standard rate. Email: contact@common-link.org
A complaint is the expression of dissatisfaction with CommonLink. It is not necessary to use the word complaint.

Any complaint may be sent by email to reclamations@common-link.org, by mail to CommonLink, Complaints Department, 1047 Chemin des Impiniers, 06220 Vallauris, France, or by phone at +33 4 23 40 02 06. A complaint made by phone that is not resolved immediately must be confirmed in writing.

CommonLink acknowledges receipt of any written complaint within a maximum of ten business days of it being sent, unless a final response is provided within that same period, and responds to it with reasons within a maximum of two months of the first written complaint being sent.
These timeframes run from when the complaint is sent, not from the date on which CommonLink becomes aware of it.

A complaint concerning a service operated by a CommonLink provider, in particular the collection of donations or the execution of a payment, is handled by CommonLink and is not referred back to that provider.
Full details are set out on the Complaints page of the site.
articles.title: Article 36. Contacting us and complaints

paragraphs: CommonLink may amend these terms, in particular to reflect changes to the service or the regulations.

Any amendment is notified to the organisation before it takes effect. An organisation that does not accept it may end these terms under the conditions of Article 33. Amendments to the financial terms are governed by Article 24.
articles.title: Article 37. Amendment of these terms

paragraphs: The computer records kept by CommonLink, in particular those relating to acceptance of these terms, campaigns, donations and payments, are conclusive evidence between the parties, unless proven otherwise.
articles.title: Article 38. Evidentiary agreement

paragraphs: If a clause of these terms is declared void or deemed unwritten, the other clauses remain fully effective.
These terms are drafted in French. In the event of translation, the French version prevails.
articles.title: Article 39. Miscellaneous provisions

paragraphs: Any question may be sent to contact@common-link.org. CommonLink endeavours to respond within two business days.
articles.title: Article 40. Contact

paragraphs: These terms are governed by French law.
The parties shall endeavour to resolve any dispute amicably. Failing that, the dispute is brought before the court with jurisdiction under ordinary law rules.

cguAssociations.title: Terms and conditions of use applicable to beneficiary organisations

paragraphs: These terms and conditions govern the use of the CommonLink service by any person who makes a donation for the benefit of an organisation present on the platform.
The relationship between CommonLink and beneficiary organisations is governed by separate terms and conditions.
The relationship between the donor and the beneficiary organisation is governed by the model agreement set out in the appendix to these terms.
articles.title: Article 1. Purpose

paragraphs: CommonLink: the company identified at the head of these terms. Site: the site accessible at www.common-link.org. Platform: the digital environment provided by CommonLink enabling beneficiary organisations to present campaigns and donors to make and track their donations. Donor: any person making a donation via the platform. Beneficiary organisation: the association or endowment fund benefiting from the donation. Campaign: the page dedicated to a fundraising operation presented by a beneficiary organisation. Donation: the payment made without consideration, with donative intent, for the benefit of an organisation.
articles.title: Article 2. Definitions

paragraphs: Acceptance of these terms is required to make a donation. It is obtained expressly, before any payment.
The model agreement set out in the appendix forms an integral part of these terms. It is accessible before acceptance, and the donor acknowledges having read it.
The accepted version, its date and time are retained.
articles.title: Article 3. Acceptance of these terms

paragraphs: CommonLink is a crowdfunding intermediary. Its role is to connect donors with organisations carrying projects of general interest, and to publish information relating to the use of donations collected.
CommonLink is not a payment institution. Payment services are provided by authorised providers.
CommonLink is not the beneficiary of the donation. It does not direct the activity of the organisations present on the platform and does not act in their place.
articles.title: Article 4. Status and role of CommonLink

paragraphs: Donations never pass through CommonLink. They are collected into an account opened in the beneficiary organisation's name with the collection provider, then transferred to its bank account.
CommonLink never receives, holds or forwards any donation. The amounts collected never appear in its accounts at any point, and it can neither appropriate them nor dispose of them.
CommonLink does not collect, store or directly process full payment card data.
articles.title: Article 5. The funds

paragraphs: The site is freely accessible to anyone with an internet connection.

CommonLink may suspend, limit or interrupt access to the site or the platform for reasons of maintenance, security or updates. It endeavours to inform users and to limit the duration of such interruptions.
articles.title: Article 6. Access to the service

paragraphs: A donation cannot be made anonymously. The donor provides their surname, first name, postal address and email address.
This information is required to issue the tax receipt and to identify the donor, as required by the regulations applicable to crowdfunding intermediaries.
The donor undertakes to provide accurate and up-to-date information.
articles.title: Article 7. Identification of the donor

paragraphs: Creating a personal account is not required to make a donation.
A donor who chooses to create one can track their donations, access their tax receipts, view the details of how funds were used for the campaigns they supported, and manage their recurring donations.
The donor is responsible for the confidentiality of their credentials. In the event of unauthorised use of their account, they must inform CommonLink without delay at contact@common-link.org
articles.title: Article 8. Personal account

paragraphs: The platform is intended for adults. A minor may only make a donation with the authorisation of their legal representative.
Donations made by legal entities are not supported at this time, as the corporate patronage tax regime uses a separate receipt form.
articles.title: Article 9. Persons who may make a donation

paragraphs: The donor chooses a campaign, an amount and a payment method. The donation is made when the payment is authorised.
Donations are made in euros. The payment methods offered are indicated at the time of donation.
articles.title: Article 10. Making a one-off donation

articles.callout: Recurring donations will be available once launched, as announced on the site. Until then, only one-off donations can be made.
paragraphs: The donor may choose to make a monthly donation for the benefit of a campaign. They are informed of the amount and date of each debit.

The donor may, at any time, from their personal account, change the amount of their recurring donation or cancel it, without reason or charge. The change or cancellation takes effect at the next due date. CommonLink cannot unilaterally change the amount of a recurring donation at any time.

When the supported campaign ends or reaches its goal, the recurring donation ends. CommonLink informs the donor and offers to allocate their donation to another project. No carry-over is made without their agreement.

When the amount remaining to reach a campaign's goal is less than the amount of the recurring donation, only the remaining amount is debited. The donor is informed at the time of the debit, and their tax receipt covers the amount actually paid.
articles.title: Article 11. Recurring donations

paragraphs: The goal displayed by a campaign is a cap. A campaign does not raise more than the need it has announced.
When this goal is reached, the campaign no longer accepts donations. A donation that would exceed this cap is not collected: the donor is informed before any payment and is offered another project.
The goal is not a threshold: the beneficiary organisation has access to the donations received even if the goal is not reached.
articles.title: Article 12. Fundraising goal

paragraphs: A donation is a voluntary and irrevocable act. It vests in the beneficiary organisation upon receipt and is not refundable.
The right of withdrawal provided for by the Consumer Code does not apply, as the beneficiary organisation is not a professional within the meaning of that code.
articles.title: Article 13. Final nature of the donation

paragraphs: The previous article does not prevent the correction of what is not a donation.
A double payment or a technical error constitutes an undue payment and gives rise to correction.

An unauthorised payment transaction, in particular in the event of fraudulent use of a payment method, is governed by the regulations applicable to payment services, and the rights the donor derives from them are not affected by these terms.
Any request should be sent to contact@common-link.org
articles.title: Article 14. Undue payments and unauthorised transactions

paragraphs: A donation made on CommonLink does not entitle the donor to any consideration, other than the tax receipt. Campaigns offering consideration to the donor are not permitted on the platform.
articles.title: Article 15. No consideration

paragraphs: The tax receipt is issued by the beneficiary organisation, which is solely responsible for its eligibility for the patronage tax regime and for the accuracy of the document.

CommonLink provides it with an issuing tool and forwards the receipt to the donor on its behalf. CommonLink does not verify the organisation's tax eligibility and guarantees neither the validity of the receipt nor the granting of a tax reduction.
The beneficiary organisation declares that it falls within the categories referred to in Articles 200 and 238 bis of the French General Tax Code.
Digital certificates and any complementary proof elements made available do not constitute tax receipts.
articles.title: Article 16. Tax receipt

paragraphs: The donor chooses whether their name appears on the campaign's public page. If they choose not to appear, their donation is counted without their identity being made public.
This choice concerns only public display. The beneficiary organisation is aware of the donor's identity, in particular to issue the tax receipt.
articles.title: Article 17. Display of the donation

paragraphs: CommonLink publishes, for each campaign, the payments made by the beneficiary organisation to its own beneficiaries, with their recipient and amount, as well as the closing report published by the organisation.

This information relates to the movements CommonLink observes. It constitutes neither an audit, nor a certification, nor a verification of the actual use of the amounts paid, which are the sole responsibility of the beneficiary organisation.
The descriptive information for a campaign, in particular its purpose, projected budget and expected outcome, is provided by the beneficiary organisation under its own responsibility.
articles.title: Article 18. Information on the use of donations

paragraphs: When a campaign is cancelled by the beneficiary organisation, or when an organisation is removed from the platform, donations already made remain vested in that organisation and are not refunded, in accordance with Article 13.
The campaign's public page remains accessible, with the information published on the use of funds as at the date of cancellation or removal.
Ongoing recurring donations end. The donors concerned are informed and offered the option to allocate their donation to another project.
articles.title: Article 19. Cancelled campaign or organisation removed from the platform

paragraphs: Use of CommonLink is free for the donor. No fee is charged to them and no amount is deducted from their donation.
CommonLink is paid by the beneficiary organisations, under the terms published on its pricing page.
articles.title: Article 20. Free of charge for the donor

paragraphs: The donor undertakes to use the site and the platform in accordance with the law and these terms.

They are in particular prohibited from using the service for fraudulent purposes, impersonating a third party, using a payment method they are not the holder of or authorised to use, disrupting the operation of the service, or circumventing its security measures.
articles.title: Article 21. Donor obligations

paragraphs: The donor's data is processed to enable the donation to be made, the tax receipt to be issued, CommonLink's legal obligations to be fulfilled and, where applicable, their personal account to be managed.
The purposes, retention periods and means of exercising your rights are set out in the privacy policy accessible on the site. Any request may be sent to contact@common-link.org
articles.title: Article 22. Personal data

paragraphs: The rules applicable to cookies and trackers are described in the cookie policy accessible on the site.
articles.title: Article 23. Cookies

paragraphs: The site, the platform, the names, distinctive signs, logos, editorial content and developments published by CommonLink are protected under intellectual property law. Any unauthorised reproduction or use is prohibited.
articles.title: Article 24. Intellectual property

paragraphs: CommonLink implements reasonable means to ensure the proper functioning of the service. It does not guarantee continuous, uninterrupted availability, as the service depends in particular on technical providers and third-party networks.
articles.title: Article 25. Availability of the service

paragraphs: The site and campaign pages may include links to sites published by third parties, in particular by beneficiary organisations.
CommonLink does not publish this content and controls neither its accuracy nor its availability.
articles.title: Article 26. Links to third-party sites

paragraphs: CommonLink undertakes to provide the service diligently, to publish the information provided for in Article 18, and to enable donations to be made under the conditions provided for in Article 5.

The service consists of connecting parties and publishing information. CommonLink does not guarantee that the project presented by a beneficiary organisation will be completed, nor the actual allocation of the amounts paid, nor the accuracy of the descriptive information it provides.

CommonLink is liable for breaches of its own obligations under ordinary law. These terms neither limit nor remove the donor's right to compensation, and do not prevent them from taking part in a class action.
articles.title: Article 27. CommonLink's undertakings and scope of the service

paragraphs: Neither party may be held liable for failure to perform its obligations resulting from a case of force majeure within the meaning of Article 1218 of the French Civil Code.
articles.title: Article 28. Force majeure

paragraphs: CommonLink may refuse a transaction, decline to act on a payment request, remove a campaign falling within an excluded case, or suspend access to its services.
These measures are reasoned and the donor is informed of them, except where the law prohibits it. They arise in particular under anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations.
articles.title: Article 29. Suspension and refusal

paragraphs: The contract entered into with a donor who has not created a personal account ends when their donation is made. The contract entered into with a donor holding a personal account is for an indefinite term.

The donor may request the closure of their personal account at any time, without reason or charge, by writing to contact@common-link.org. Closure is carried out within thirty days of the request and confirmed by email.
Closure ends any ongoing recurring donations as of the next due date. It has no effect on donations already made, which remain final.

Closure does not result in the immediate deletion of the donor's data. CommonLink retains what the law requires it to keep, in particular for five years under its anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations, and for tax receipts issued in its name. Once these periods expire, the data is deleted. Beneficiary organisations retain, for their part, the data necessary for their own obligations.

complaints.intro: You are not satisfied with a service provided by CommonLink, with information you received, or with how your request was handled. This page explains how to let us know and what happens next.

paragraphs: A complaint is the expression of dissatisfaction with us. You don’t need to use the word "complaint," or to ask for anything in particular.
You also don't need to have made a donation, or to have an account. Anyone can send us a complaint.
On the other hand, a request for information, an explanation, or assistance is not a complaint. For these requests, simply write to us at contact@common-link.org

We respond to you in writing, with reasons, within a maximum of two months.

The crowdfunding intermediary activity is subject to the supervision of the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR).
CommonLink never receives the donations collected.
sections.title: Regulatory status

paragraphs: Donations never pass through CommonLink. Each association has an account opened in its name with Mollie, an electronic money institution authorised in the Netherlands and supervised by the Dutch central bank. Donations are collected there on the association's behalf, in funds ring-fenced and kept separate from Mollie's own funds, then transferred to its bank account.
CommonLink never receives, holds or forwards any donation. The amounts collected never appear in its accounts at any point, and it can neither appropriate them nor dispose of them.
CommonLink is paid by the association by means of a monthly invoice, settled separately from donations. No amount is deducted from the donations collected.

When an association pays a beneficiary from the platform, the transfer is made from its own bank account, through Bridge, a payment institution authorised by the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority under number 16918. It is authorised by the association's legal representative, who authenticates with their bank. Neither CommonLink nor Bridge hold the funds at any point. CommonLink cannot trigger this transfer in place of the legal representative, nor cancel it once it has been authorised.
sections.title: Circulation of funds

articles.title: 1. Purpose of the donation

articles.title: 2. Final nature of the donation

paragraphs: The donor acquires no rights over the funded project. They cannot demand its completion, claim a share of its results, request the return of their donation, or obtain any form of consideration.
articles.title: 3. No rights over the project

paragraphs: The beneficiary organisation undertakes to account for the use of collected funds, by making the payments funded by the campaign from the platform and by publishing a report at its closing.
This undertaking is an information obligation. It constitutes neither a guarantee that the project will be completed nor an obligation of result.
articles.title: 4. The organisation's duty to account

paragraphs: The beneficiary organisation issues the tax receipt. It is solely responsible for its eligibility for the patronage tax regime and for the accuracy of the document.

CommonLink provides it with an issuing tool and forwards the receipt to the donor on its behalf. It does not verify the organisation’s eligibility and guarantees neither the validity of the receipt nor the granting of a tax reduction.
articles.title: 5. Tax receipt

paragraphs: Amounts paid by the donor are collected into an account opened in the beneficiary organisation's name, then transferred to its bank account. They never pass through CommonLink.

paragraphs: The beneficiary organisation is aware of the donor's identity, in particular to issue their tax receipt. It may make no other use of it than those related to this obligation and to its relationship with its donors.

fonds.callout: A campaign's goal is not a threshold to cross. An association that has raised €8,000 out of a €10,000 goal has those €8,000 and can use them as soon as they are transferred. A donation belongs to it as soon as it is received.
fonds.capText1: The goal is also a cap. A campaign does not raise more than the need it announced.
fonds.capText2: Once the cap is reached, the campaign no longer accepts donations. A donation that would exceed this cap is not collected: you are informed before any payment, and we suggest another project from the same association or a comparable one.
fonds.closeText1: The association publishes a closing report accounting for the use of funds.
fonds.closeText2: If part of the funds was not spent, for example because the project cost less than expected, those funds remain the association's, and it states in its report what it does with them. They are not returned to donors: a donation is final as soon as it is received.

fonds.spendText1: A campaign’s expenses are charged against donations received in the order they arrived, oldest first.
fonds.spendText2: An association can only commit, from CommonLink, the amounts actually available for the campaign in question.
